options.label: New module in ai-harness (Recommended)
options.description: New top-level dir (e.g. perm_gate_lab/) next to remote_control/ and manager/. Reuses your skills, supervisor, settings, and the existing PreToolUse hook can write straight into its log. Lowest friction.

options.label: Brand-new standalone repo
options.description: Fresh repo on its own. Cleanest separation, but you re-do CI, settings.json wiring, project board, and the hook has to cross a repo boundary to log decisions.

options.label: Submodule of perm_gate
options.description: Lives under the existing perm_gate code in ai-harness. Tight coupling — fine if you see the lab as part of perm_gate forever, awkward if it grows independent.

questions.question: How should the review UI be served?

options.label: New tab inside manager-ui on :8765 (Recommended)
options.description: Reuse the launchd-managed FastAPI app you already have. One process, one auth story, sessions and perm-gate decisions side-by-side.

options.label: Separate FastAPI app on its own port
options.description: New launchd service, e.g. :8766. Cleaner separation of concerns; double the ops surface (two services to keep alive, two URLs to remember).

options.label: CLI + static HTML report
options.description: No long-running server. Generate static pages from the log on demand. Simpler, but no live review, no labelling UI.

questions.question: What goes into the captured corpus?

options.label: Your PreToolUse hook (static + AI tier)
options.description: Every tool-call the hook sees, with its tier, rule fired, AI rationale if any, final verdict. This is the bedrock.

options.label: Anthropic Auto Mode decisions (if exposed)
options.description: If Auto Mode surfaces its classifier verdict via transcript or API, capture it alongside yours. Lets you compare your judge vs Anthropic's on the same situation. May not be observable today.

options.label: Human overrides / corrections
options.description: When the user accepts/denies a prompt the system asked about, log that as ground-truth feedback. Critical for the scoring side later.

options.label: Synthetic adversarial cases
options.description: Curated red-team prompts (rm -rf /, exfil via curl, prompt-injection patterns). Lets you regression-test even when real traffic is quiet.

questions.question: How do new guidelines get a 'score'?

options.label: Human-labeled ground truth (Recommended)
options.description: You (or a reviewer) tag captured cases with the ideal verdict + risk rating. New guideline runs are scored by agreement with labels (precision/recall on deny, false-allow rate on red, etc.). Most rigorous.

options.label: Champion-vs-challenger only
options.description: No human labels. New guideline is scored by where it disagrees with a designated 'champion' run. Cheap to bootstrap, but you can drift — both can be wrong together.

options.label: LLM-as-judge
options.description: A separate Claude call grades each (case, verdict) pair. Fast and scalable, but the judge has its own biases and you've added a second model to trust.

options.label: Hybrid: labels where you have them, LLM-judge elsewhere
options.description: Start with champion+LLM-judge, layer human labels on top as you accumulate them. Most pragmatic; more moving parts.

transcript_tail.text: Can you search the web for it because a friend told me Claude could already have it?

Your friend is right — Anthropic shipped **Claude Code Auto Mode** on March 24, 2026. It's almost exactly the design pattern of your local `PERM_GATE`:

- An AI classifier (Sonnet 4.6) reviews every tool call before execution
- Routes to one of three outcomes: **auto-approve / prompt / block**
- Looks at action type, parameters, reversibility, and blast radius
- Specifically watches for mass deletions, secret exfiltration, and prompt-injection-style malicious patterns
- Positioned as the middle ground between manual approval and `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
- Anthropic is explicit it's **not a security boundary** — it's a mistake-prevention layer

**Availability**: launched on Team plans first, admin opt-in required; Enterprise + API "coming soon."

So the relationship to your work:

- Your ai-harness#23 perm gate predates it (yours is a `PreToolUse` hook, currently static-only with `PERM_GATE_ENFORCE_AI=1` not yet flipped).
- Anthropic's version is in-app, hosted, and uses Sonnet 4.6 as the classifier.
- The two can coexist — `PreToolUse` hooks fire regardless of Auto Mode — so you could keep your static red-list (`rm -rf /`, etc.) as a hard floor under whatever Auto Mode decides.

Worth checking if your plan tier has Auto Mode available before you invest more in `ENFORCE_AI` — might be cheaper to delegate the AI tier to Anthropic and keep your hook for the static/red rules and the deny-list tuning tracked in #25.

Sources:
- [Claude Code auto mode: a safer way to skip permissions (Anthropic)](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-auto-mode)
- [What Is Claude Code Auto Mode? How the Permission Classifier Works (MindStudio)](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/what-is-claude-code-auto-mode-permission-classifier)
- [Inside Claude Code Auto Mode (InfoQ)](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/05/anthropic-claude-code-auto-mode/)
- [Anthropic trims action approval loop (Help Net Security)](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/25/anthropic-claude-code-auto-mode-feature/)
- [Claude Code Auto Approve Guide 2026 (SmartScope)](https://smartscope.blog/en/generative-ai/claude/claude-code-auto-permission-guide/)

Good news — Max plan **has** Auto Mode as of mid-April 2026.

Specifics for your setup:
- **Available directly** — no admin enablement needed (that's a Team/Enterprise hoop)
- **Model requirement on Max**: **Opus 4.7** (you're already on it — see your environment header)
- Toggle it in Claude Code itself; not a CLI flag

A couple of caveats worth knowing before you flip it on:
- There were intermittent "Auto mode is unavailable for your plan" bugs reported on Max as recently as the issues above — if you see that, it's a known bug, not a license problem.
- Anthropic still says it's a **mistake-prevention** layer, not a security boundary. Your `PreToolUse` perm-gate hook keeps running underneath it, so your static red-list (`rm -rf /`, push-to-main, etc.) stays as the hard floor.

Want me to check whether enabling it would conflict with your current `PERM_GATE_ENFORCE=1` hook — i.e. whether the two layers fight or stack cleanly?

Sources:
- [Claude Code Auto Mode: Now on Max, Team, and Enterprise (claudefa.st)](https://claudefa.st/blog/guide/development/auto-mode)
- [Feature request: Make auto mode available on Max plan (closed) — anthropics/claude-code#41219](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/41219)
- [Max plan: "auto mode is not available for your plan" — anthropics/claude-code#46616](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/46616)
- [Use Claude Code with your Pro or Max plan (Anthropic Help Center)](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11145838-use-claude-code-with-your-pro-or-max-plan)
